citations.narrative:
The facility is not maintaining the indoor shift doors for the Colobus monkeys; the metal grates over the gates are not free
of excessive rust. There are large areas of the metal grates that are a reddish brown. The Colobus monkeys can come
into contact with the rusted surfaces. Rusted primary enclosure surfaces can lose structural integrity over time and cannot
be properly cleaned and sanitized. The licensee must ensure that any surfaces that come into contact with non-human
primates are free of excessive rust that prevents the required cleaning and sanitization, or that affects the structural
strength of the surfaces.
Corrected prior to delivery of the inspection report.

The surfaces of the primary enclosure for 2 Green-Winged Macaws are not free of rust. The metal wiring that acts as a
screen between the Green-Winged Macaws and the Military Macaw enclosures has lost its protective covering and has
widespread rust. Over 80% of the wire screen is affected. Excessive rust can compromise the structural strength, create
rough and jagged surfaces that could injure the birds, and prevent proper cleaning and sanitization, increasing the risk of
contamination and disease. The surfaces of housing facilities must be constructed in a manner and made of materials that
allow them to be readily cleaned and/or sanitized, or removed and replaced when worn or soiled. Interior surfaces and
surfaces that come in contact with birds must be: Free of rust or damage that affects the structural integrity of the surface
or prevents cleaning.
Corrected prior to delivery of inspection report.

The indoor enclosure platform for the King Vultures is not being maintained so as to prevent harm to the birds. One of the
wooden boards that makes up the border of the structure was damaged and had missing sections on the interior aspect of
the wood. A metal bolt was visible in the damaged section. The platform normally holds an igloo shelter that was being
cleaned at the time of the inspection and obscures this section of the platform. Damaged wood used in bird platforms can
lead to injuries to the birds and potentially affect the integrity of the platform itself. Furniture-type objects, such as perches
and other objects that enrich a bird’s environment, must be species-appropriate and be designed, constructed, and
maintained so as to prevent harm to the bird.
Corrected prior to delivery of the inspection report.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
